newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end down, but up from lows.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end down, but up from lows.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rallied in late trade to settle near their daily highs, but still ended lower on the day in line with weaker cash prices, market sources said Wednesday.

Traders noted the September contracts for both California-Oregon border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) electricity managed to stay above trendline support of $22.43 per megawatt (MWh) and $29.19, respectively.
"They threatened to break through support, but they did not manage to drop that far," noted one dealer.
But traders said market fundamentals indicate further price erosion for the power futures complex.
"I expect them to come off again tomorrow and trade below support," the dealer said.
He cited plenty of hydroelectric power supplies in the Northwest, which saw the highest runoff on record in the season ending July 31.

"Once the Intertie is corrected, more power can be transferred to the Northwest," noted another trader, referring to maintenance-related cutbacks on the transmission system linking the Northwest to Southern California.
The Intertie maintenance is scheduled to continue through Thursday night.
Traders also cited forecasts of continued mild weather in the Southwest as a bearish factor for power futures.

For the Southwest next week, forecasters called for above normal temperatures only for southeastern sections. Near normal readings were expected for central areas, and below normal temperatures were seen for the north and west.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average below normal next week, with western areas forecast to see well below normal readings.
The September PV contract lost 55 cents to close at $29.96 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with a low for the day of $29.30 and a high of $30.25.
October PV also fell 55 cents to settle at $22.94, while November was down 34 cents at $22.50.
COB for September closed 13 cents lower at $22.97, compared with a high for the day of $23.00 and a low of $22.50.
October COB lost 47 cents to close at $22.33. November COB fell 30 cents to $23.00 and December fell 60 cents to $24.70.
In generation news, a 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired plant in Washington state was expected to be back on line late Wednesday after shutting Monday for repairs.
A 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was restarted as expected late Tuesday after being shut Friday for unplanned repairs.
A 750 MW unit at the Navajo coal-fired plant in Arizona was back up by early Wednesday after shutting over the weekend for repairs.
NYMEX estimated 595 COB and 334 PV contracts were sold as of 1533 EDT Wednesday.
((--Los Angeles bureau +1 213 955 6761))
